name: Chorus Wash
description: The chorus program: a short cluster of wandering delays rather than a reverb. Widens and thickens a guitar or a synth.

name: Chamber
description: The chamber: dense at once and warm, with no gap before it. For drums and guitars that want a room around them.

name: Constant Plate
description: The constant plate: the same time at every frequency, short and dense. A plate that stays out of the way.

name: Eighties Snare Hall
description: The small hall with a short middle and long lows, sent loud: the big snare of the mid-1980s.

name: Infinite Pad
description: The large hall at sixteen seconds in the middle and longer below, its delays wandering slowly: a wash that hangs under a pad or a drone.

name: Large Hall
description: The large hall: a bigger loop, a slower build, and a long dark tail for pads, ballads, and orchestral parts.

name: Percussion Plate
description: The percussion plate: diffused hard so a snare or a clap blooms at once into a smooth wash.

name: Room
description: The room: under two seconds, its top falling early. Puts drums and percussion in a space without washing them.

name: Small Hall A
description: The first small hall as the unit loads it: three seconds in the bass, two in the middle, dark above 6.6 kHz. The digital hall of 1980s records, for vocals, strings, and a mix's send.

name: Small Hall B
description: The second small hall: its treble shorter and its diffusion lower, so the tail is darker and its first echoes more distinct.

name: Vocal Plate
description: The vocal plate: bright to the converters' edge and even across the bands, with no gap; the plate sound for a lead vocal.
